opponents.overview_text: Curtis Vasquez is a current Talmadge County Commissioner running for Rockvale City Council. He is a policy expert, volunteer firefighter, and community organizer with more than two decades of experience in public service and advocacy. His campaign centers on post-disaster resilience, housing affordability, and support for small businesses and the arts. He holds endorsements from multiple state legislators, county officials, and civic leaders.
opponents.background_text: Vasquez currently serves as Talmadge County Commissioner. He holds a Master's degree in Public Administration from American University and a B.A. in Political Science from Georgia State. He works as the Southeast Campaigns Director for the Natural Resources Defense Council and previously served as Director of Environment Georgia, with additional roles at the Longview Trail Conservancy, the Sierra Club, and the Georgia General Assembly. opponents.overview_text: Elias Marchetti is a former Rockvale City Council member with five years of council service. His campaign runs on a governance record that includes launching a $74 million bond initiative, establishing the Department of Equity and Inclusion, creating the Human Relations Commission, and shaping Rockvale's municipal reparations framework. His campaign slogan is 'Focused on You' and frames the race as a choice between governance and advocacy.
opponents.background_text: Marchetti served five years on the Rockvale City Council. His campaign credits him with leading the creation of the city's Department of Equity and Inclusion, initiating the Human Relations Commission, and serving as what his campaign describes as the architect of Rockvale's municipal reparations framework and reparations commission. He led the effort to catalog city-owned land into a public database and assembled the council majority needed to advance a $74 million bond -- described on his site as the largest infrastructure investment in Rockvale's history -- covering road paving, water and storm drain repair, the Foundry Arts District Transportation Improvement Project, Centennial Stadium restoration, and the Grant Center. His initiatives also include a citywide emergency telephone notification system and a policy that reduced the city's default water bill payment rate by approximately 90 percent, along with raising all city workers to a living wage, advancing Ban the Box policy, and minority- and women-owned business contracting reforms. He is a Soros Equality Fellow, co-founder of the Government Accountability Project Rockvale and the Reparations Stakeholder Authority of Rockvale, and founder of the Marchetti Foundation for Social Justice and the Arts. He is an award-winning filmmaker whose documentary Architects of Change is described as Academy Award-qualifying. He is a graduate of Virginia State University and completed executive education at Harvard Kennedy School.
issues_that_matter: Hurricane recovery and resilient infrastructure rebuilding
Housing affordability and stability through coordinated, practical policy
Accountable and transparent city governance with measurable outcomes
Fairness, equity, and civil rights protections embedded in city operations
Workforce development, living wages, and equitable public contracting
Long-term infrastructure maintenance and capital planning

opponents.overview_text: Rosalind Ferraro is the incumbent Vice Mayor of Rockvale, an attorney, and a lifelong resident running for re-election. Affordable housing and protecting legacy neighborhoods from displacement
Downtown safety and neighborhood vitality
Local arts, culture, and community spaces
Equity and inclusion for residents underserved by government

issues.title: Flood Resilience and Infrastructure

issues.description: Cut red tape for local entrepreneurs, create a small business relief fund, and push back against commercial rent increases that are pricing out longtime local shops.
